clue.text: The president once responsible for Chelsea getting smashed and going round breaking law

indicators.note: going round means the reworked Chelsea surrounds the other piece
smashed means broken to pieces, so the letters of Chelsea are rearranged
breaking a word up means its letters are jumbled, here the letters of law

explanation.surface: A former US president who fathered Chelsea is pictured drunk and lawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Bill Clinton, Chelsea's father, but the president is Polish. 'Getting smashed' turns Chelsea into LECHESA, 'breaking' turns law into WAL, and 'going round' puts LECHESA round WAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lech Walesa, the Solidarity leader, was President of Poland from 1990 to 1995.

clue.text: Fast mover, also known as 'Coach', is getting screwed

parts.note: a coach is a bus

indicators.note: a screw is twisted round, so the word is is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Someone nicknamed Coach is being cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting screwed' twists is round to SI, as a screw turns. Kriss Akabusi was a British Olympic hurdler and sprinter of the 1980s and 90s, and this grid spells his name with a double S.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion hurdler and relay runner is a fast mover in the most literal sense.

clue.text: Revolutionaries' sudden movements

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., short for Trotskyists, the far-left revolutionaries
second meaning: slang for diarrhoea, urgent movements of the bowels

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves look like one phrase about revolutionaries acting suddenly; the second is a lavatory joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for followers of Trotsky and a slang name for diarrhoea.

clue.text: Hard to get in car, yes, where your butt gets crushed?

indicators.note: to get in means the letter for hard goes inside the car's name

parts.note: the Astra is a Vauxhall car model
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Squeezing into a cramped car leaves your backside squashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' suggests your backside, but it is a cigarette end. 'To get in' puts H inside the Vauxhall ASTRA to make ASHTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokers stub out cigarette ends in this small dish, so it is where a butt is crushed.

clue.text: Be horribly ill going round clubs — something the Eye's familiar with!

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so the letters of be and ill are mixed
whirling round, adding to the sense that the letters are spun into a new order

parts.note: clubs is one suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Feeling dreadful while doing the rounds of nightclubs, something Private Eye knows well.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine famously sued many times for defamation. 'going round clubs' reads as a pub crawl, but clubs is just the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye has faced many defamation actions in court over its satire, so such litigation is all too familiar.

clue.text: Definitive UN agency for old rockers

parts.note: the is the definite article, so definitive is a playful way to clue it
WHO is the World Health Organization, a United Nations agency

explanation.surface: A United Nations agency is said to be the last word on veteran rock musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Who are a veteran 1960s British rock band, so they are old rockers.

clue.text: She kept her head, making Norm run

parts.note: par is the norm or standard
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A woman stays calm and makes a man called Norm run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept her head' sounds like staying calm, but it is literal: Catherine Parr, Henry VIII's last wife, outlived him and was never beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Parr survived Henry VIII, unlike two earlier wives who were executed.

clue.text: Member kept up bravely

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for the penis
second meaning: from the British idiom keep your ... up, meaning stay cheerful and brave

explanation.walkthrough: Typical Private Eye smut: the idiom 'keep your pecker up' (stay brave) also means something rude.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for the male organ and is also the thing kept up in the idiom about staying courageous.

clue.text: Just like Ms O'Connor entered by Kelvin and later injected with heroin

definitions.text: Just like Ms O'Connor entered by Kelvin and later injected with heroin

indicators.note: entered by means the next letter goes inside the name
later injected with means a second letter is inserted after the first

parts.note: Sinead O'Connor, the Irish singer famous for her shaven head
H is slang for heroin
K is the symbol for kelvin, the temperature unit

explanation.surface: The singer Sinead O'Connor gets mixed up with a man named Kelvin and drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The name does double duty: her shaven look is the definition, and her name is the fodder. 'Later injected with' puts H into SINEAD to make SINHEAD, and 'entered by' then puts K inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinead O'Connor shaved her head, giving her the cropped look of a skinhead.

clue.text: 'Hello sailor' inside crap furniture store

indicators.note: inside means sailor goes within the greeting

parts.note: hi is an informal hello
AB is able seaman, a sailor
tat is cheap rubbish, or crap

explanation.surface: A camp sailor's greeting is heard among the rubbish in a furniture shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hello sailor' is a British camp catchphrase, but here the two words are split: 'inside' puts the sailor within the greeting, making HABI. Habitat is a British chain selling furniture and home goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitat is a well-known British chain of shops selling furniture and homeware.

clue.text: Theatre Royal hack joins battle with Penny

parts.note: ed is short for editor, and a hack is a journalist
a war is a battle on a large scale
d is the old abbreviation for a penny, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A journalist covering the Theatre Royal goes to war with a woman called Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre Royal' looks like a playhouse name but is the definition: Prince Edward left the Marines to work in theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Edward worked for Andrew Lloyd Webber's theatre company, making him the royal of the theatre world.

clue.text: Corporation owner dripping with money paid into bank account regularly

parts.note: dripping is fat left from roasting meat

parts.words: money paid into bank account regularly
parts.note: SO stands for standing order, an instruction to pay money in regularly

explanation.surface: A rich company owner is flush with money coming steadily into his account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company, but it is old slang for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporation is jocular slang for a paunch, so the person who has one is a fat person.

clue.text: An opportunity, with lots of others, to get your member out and maybe get some action?

definitions.text: An opportunity, with lots of others, to get your member out and maybe get some action?

parts.words: An opportunity, with lots of others, to get your member out and maybe get some action?
parts.note: reads like an orgy, but describes many voters calling their Member of Parliament out to press for change

explanation.walkthrough: The member is your MP: at a mass lobby crowds of constituents call MPs out of the Commons to demand action.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass lobby is a large organised gathering of people meeting their MPs at Parliament to press a cause.

clue.text: A model of inflation that satisfies some?

definitions.text: A model of inflation that satisfies some?

parts.words: A model of inflation that satisfies some?
parts.note: reads like economics, but means an inflatable figure used for sex

explanation.walkthrough: 'Model of inflation' sounds like an economic forecast; it is a figure you blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an inflatable life-size figure of a person, sold as a sex toy.

clue.text: Dummy who gets fired for failing to give MPs a rise?

definitions.text: Dummy who gets fired for failing to give MPs a rise?

parts.words: Dummy who gets fired for failing to give MPs a rise?
parts.note: reads like a sacked minister, but means the stuffed figure burned on Bonfire Night

explanation.walkthrough: The plotter of 1605 failed to blow Parliament sky-high; effigies of him, called guys, are burned every 5 November.
explanation.definitionFit: Effigies of the Gunpowder Plot conspirator are set on bonfires in Britain each November.

clue.text: In their bungling way, can't they see the funny side of screwing people for cash?

definitions.text: In their bungling way, can't they see the funny side of screwing people for cash?

parts.words: In their bungling way, can't they see the funny side of screwing people for cash?
parts.note: the clumsy investigators of financial swindles, whose name says they are not joking about it

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the first word of the name: the agency is never laughing about swindles. It is the UK body that prosecutes major fraud, often mocked for losing cases.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK agency investigating serious and complex fraud is literally named as not seeing the funny side.

clue.text: Two Barbaras — old flames as far as Brenda's concerned?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the surnames of two famous Barbaras, the Carry On actress and the Labour cabinet minister

definitions.text: old flames as far as Brenda's concerned?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the royal residence that burned in 1992

explanation.surface: Two women named Barbara are former lovers of someone called Brenda.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen. Her home Windsor Castle burned in November 1992, so it is an 'old flame'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fire at the Queen's castle in 1992 makes it, jokingly, a past blaze in her life.

clue.text: Dozy party member from Lewis

parts.note: reads like a sleepy politician, but means the sleepy guest at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Lewis Carroll

explanation.walkthrough: 'Party member' suggests politics; the party is the tea party in Alice in Wonderland, by Lewis Carroll.
explanation.definitionFit: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the small rodent keeps falling asleep at the tea party.

clue.text: Drug transport

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the dance drug MDMA
second meaning: a transport of delight, rapture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug transport' reads as smuggling, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the club drug MDMA and also an overwhelming feeling of joy.

clue.text: Currently to be found under Portillo, wife gets dodgy CIA offer

definitions.text: Currently to be found under Portillo

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Michael Portillo's wife is said to receive a shady proposal from the CIA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges W and CIA OFFER. Michael Portillo was the British Defence Secretary in the mid-1990s, so the department of war was then under him.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for the government department running the army describes the ministry Portillo headed.

clue.text: See 16
See 16
In the middle of Cher arrangement model has to vomit

indicators.note: in the middle of means the next letter sits inside the reworked name
an arrangement of letters is a new order of them, so the letters of Cher are rearranged

parts.note: the Model T was the Ford car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A model is sick partway through a song arranged for the singer Cher.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave or try to vomit, a near synonym.

clue.text: Arsehole inadequate? Should keep you off the streets

definitions.text: Should keep you off the streets

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible person
few means not enough

explanation.surface: An insult about a bottom being too small, then advice on staying out of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is an order requiring people to stay indoors after a set hour.

clue.text: Part of your member left inside woman

indicators.note: inside means left goes within the name

parts.note: Una is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A rude picture of part of a man's member left inside a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' is a limb here, the arm, not the usual Cyclops meaning. 'Inside' puts L within UNA.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two bones of the forearm, and an arm is a limb.

clue.text: All people long to be disassociated from such a naff programme!

indicators.note: to be disassociated from means the letter is cut away from the phrase

parts.note: the world means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone wants nothing to do with a dreadful TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be disassociated from' takes L out of THE WORLD. The Word was a notoriously crass Channel 4 late-night show of the early 1990s; naff is British slang for tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: The Channel 4 youth show was widely mocked as tasteless and trashy.

clue.text: Computer memory thieves' briefs

parts.note: K stands for a kilobyte of computer memory
nickers are thieves, from nick meaning to steal

explanation.surface: Computer data stolen and the short legal papers of thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefs' looks like lawyers' briefs; it is underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs and knickers are both words for short underpants.

clue.text: See 17
